regulation_clause.text: Explicit consent is required to adjust credit (from refund/failed/reversed transactions already paid for) beyond a cut-off of one percent of the credit limit or Rs 5000, whichever is lower; consent sought within 7 days of the credit; on cardholder request, reversal to the bank account within 3 working days.

prediction.rationale: Clause 31 sets the cutoff to min(one percent of the credit limit, Rs 5,000). XCHTP08.cpy supplies 6,000 as the cap; XCHT08.cbl uses the percentage-or-cap calculation and routes amounts above the resulting threshold to consent. When one percent exceeds 6,000, this implementation can adjust credits between Rs 5,000 and Rs 6,000 without consent.

model_responses.final_answer: The clause sets the cutoff at the lower of one percent of the credit limit and Rs 5,000. XCHTP08.cpy sets the cap to 6,000, and XCHT08.cbl uses that cap when calculating the adjustment threshold, so a 5,500 credit can be adjusted without consent when one percent exceeds 6,000. This is a cutoff boundary error.

regulation_clause.text: Explicit consent is required to adjust credit (from refund/failed/reversed transactions already paid for) beyond a cut-off of one percent of the credit limit or Rs 5000, whichever is lower; consent sought within 7 days of the credit; on cardholder request, reversal to the bank account within 3 working days.

prediction.rationale: Clause 31 sets the cutoff to min(one percent of the credit limit, Rs 5,000). XCLYP10.cpy supplies 6,000 as the cap; XCLY10.cbl uses the percentage-or-cap calculation and routes amounts above the resulting threshold to consent. When one percent exceeds 6,000, this implementation can adjust credits between Rs 5,000 and Rs 6,000 without consent.

exec_probe.description: With a credit limit of 1,000,000, the one-percent amount is above both caps. This probes whether the 6,000 cap lets a 5,500 credit take the adjustment path.

model_responses.final_answer: The clause sets the cutoff at the lower of one percent of the credit limit and Rs 5,000. XCLYP10.cpy sets the cap to 6,000, and XCLY10.cbl uses that cap when calculating the adjustment threshold, so a 5,500 credit can be adjusted without consent when one percent exceeds 6,000. This is a cutoff boundary error.
